sentence_stem: My little brother can't read yet, so
correct_completion: his teacher reads the story to him.
full_sentence: My little brother can't read yet, so his teacher reads the story to him.
acceptable_variants: his mother reads the story to him.
he listens to an audio story instead.

options.text: he can read every book in the house.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts 'can't read yet', so it cannot follow the stem as a logical result.

options.text: his teacher reads the story to him.
he can swim across the lake.
options.why_wrong: This states another ability, but it does not explain what happens because he cannot read.

options.text: he likes to play football after school.
options.why_wrong: This gives a fact about his hobbies, but it does not describe the result of his inability to read.

grammar_focus: Can / can't for ability, with 'so' introducing a result
explanation: 'Can't' states a lack of ability, so the clause after 'so' must describe the result of that lack. Polish speakers may add a second negative after can't, so keep the negation only once in the verb phrase.
translation: Mój młodszy brat jeszcze nie potrafi czytać, więc jego nauczyciel czyta mu historię.
